title: Senior's toolkit: building images
summary: The build flags, cache mounts, multi-platform builds and image checks used to ship fast, small, safe images.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: building images
steps.body: Builds that take ten minutes, images that will not run on the server, a critical CVE in the base image: these commands fix the everyday image problems.

toolkit.what: Builds an image from the Dockerfile in the current folder (the build context) and tags it.
flags: stop at a named stage (tests, debugging)

toolkit.what: Shows every line of every step, and with `--no-cache` reruns them all. The way to see why a step fails or which step busts the cache.
flags: full output instead of the collapsing view
toolkit.when: a step fails in CI but you cannot see why

toolkit.what: Keeps a package cache (NuGet, npm, apt) between builds without putting it in the image. Restores take seconds instead of minutes.
flags: where the tool keeps its cache, for example `/root/.nuget/packages`
mount a secret for one step, never stored in a layer

toolkit.what: Builds one image for several CPU types. Needed when people build on Apple silicon (arm64) and servers run amd64.
flags: push the multi-platform result to the registry
reuse the build cache in GitHub Actions

toolkit.what: Shows each layer, its size and the instruction that made it. Finds the step that made the image huge.
Lists known vulnerabilities in the image's packages. Trivy is the common open-source equivalent in CI.
flags: fail a CI step on serious findings

toolkit.what: Shows untagged leftover images from rebuilds, which quietly eat disk space.

steps.prompt: An image built on a MacBook with an M-series chip works there. On the amd64 build server it fails immediately with `exec format error`. What fixes it?
options: Build for the server's platform: `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 ... --push`
steps.explain: `exec format error` means the binaries are for another CPU. The Mac built arm64; the server needs amd64. Build a multi-platform image (or at least `--platform linux/amd64`).

steps.prompt: Every build runs `dotnet restore` for four minutes, even when you changed one line of C#. `--progress=plain` shows `COPY . .` right before the restore. What is the fix?
options: Copy only the `.csproj` files, run `restore`, then `COPY . .`; add a cache mount for `/root/.nuget/packages`
steps.explain: Any source change busts the cache for every step after `COPY . .`. Copying project files first lets the restore layer be reused, and the cache mount makes a real restore fast too.

steps.prompt: Build only up to the `build` stage, with full step output, and tag it.
steps.explain: `--target` picks the stage by its `AS` name; `--progress=plain` prints every line; `-t` tags. There is no `--stage` flag.

steps.prompt: Match each problem to the tool that answers it.
pairs: Which layer made the image 1.2 GB?
Does the base image have a critical CVE?
Why did step 7 fail in CI?
Servers need amd64, laptops make arm64
NuGet restore is slow on every build

steps.prompt: Safe way to give a build a value, or a leak?
buckets: Ends up in the image or its history

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: When a build is slow or broken, rerun it with `--progress=plain` and read which step reruns. Scan every image you push with `trivy` or `docker scout` in CI, and build `--platform` explicitly so laptops and servers never disagree.
